ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 5.1: Leadership and commitment
rationale: Clause 5.1 requires top management to demonstrate leadership and commitment by setting policy and objectives, providing resources, and promoting continual improvement. Top Management Commitment is that visible, resourced leadership of the management system.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 5.3: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities; A.5.2: Information security roles and responsibilities
rationale: Clause 5.3 requires roles, responsibilities, and authorities for the ISMS to be assigned and communicated, and A.5.2 requires security responsibilities to be defined and allocated. Charters & Committees formalizes the oversight bodies and the authority each holds.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 5.1: Leadership and commitment; 9.3: Management review
rationale: Clause 5.1 places accountability for ISMS effectiveness with top management and 9.3 requires management review of ISMS performance at planned intervals. Executive Leadership & Board Oversight supplies the governing-body review of risk posture and compliance that these clauses require.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.10: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets; A.6.2: Terms and conditions of employment
rationale: A.5.10 requires rules for acceptable use of information and assets to be identified, documented, and implemented, and A.6.2 requires employment terms to state security responsibilities. COC: Acceptable Use is the rule set personnel acknowledge and follow.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 5.2: Policy; A.5.1: Policies for information security
rationale: Clause 5.2 requires top management to establish an information security policy appropriate to the organization, and A.5.1 requires policies and topic-specific policies to be defined, approved, published, communicated, and reviewed. Core Policies provides and governs that policy suite.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.1: Policies for information security; A.5.37: Documented operating procedures
rationale: A.5.1 requires topic-specific information security policies, and A.5.37 requires documented operating procedures. Security Policies defines the enforceable confidentiality, integrity, and availability expectations that these documents express.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity
rationale: A.5.24 requires incident management to be planned and prepared, A.5.29 requires planning for maintaining information security during disruption, and A.5.30 requires ICT continuity to be planned, implemented, and tested. Response & Resilience Policies is the policy basis for IR, BCP, and DR.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.1: Policies for information security
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.1 requires topic-specific policies, which can include an AI policy, but ISO/IEC 27001 has no AI-specific requirement. AI Policies satisfies A.5.1 only to the extent AI systems are in ISMS scope; ISO/IEC 42001 is the closer standard.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.34 requires privacy and PII protection requirements to be identified and met. Privacy Policies defines the rules for lawful processing that satisfy the policy part of A.5.34; ISO/IEC 27701 covers privacy policy in depth.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.6.1: Screening; A.6.2: Terms and conditions of employment; A.6.5: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment; A.6.6: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
rationale: A.6.1 requires background screening, A.6.2 requires security responsibilities in employment terms, A.6.5 requires responsibilities after termination or change, and A.6.6 requires confidentiality agreements. HR Policies sets these personnel requirements across the employee lifecycle.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.19: Information security in supplier relationships; A.5.20: Addressing information security within supplier agreements; A.5.21: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
rationale: A.5.19 requires processes to manage supplier security risk, A.5.20 requires security requirements in supplier agreements, and A.5.21 requires management of ICT supply chain risk. Supply-Chain Policies sets the security, privacy, and ethical standards suppliers must meet.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.9: Inventory of information and other associated assets; A.5.10: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets; A.5.12: Classification of information; A.5.13: Labelling of information; A.5.14: Information transfer; A.5.33: Protection of records
rationale: A.5.9 requires an asset inventory, A.5.10 acceptable use rules, A.5.12 and A.5.13 classification and labelling, A.5.14 information transfer rules, and A.5.33 protection of records. Data-Governance Policies sets the lifecycle, quality, and handling rules these controls require.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.1: Policies for information security; A.5.36: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
rationale: A.5.1 requires policies to be implemented through supporting rules, and A.5.36 requires compliance with policies, rules, and standards to be regularly reviewed. Core Standards translates policy into measurable standards against which A.5.36 compliance is checked.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.1: User endpoint devices; A.8.2: Privileged access rights; A.8.3: Information access restriction; A.8.9: Configuration management
rationale: A.8.9 requires configurations, including security configurations, to be established and maintained, and A.8.1 to A.8.3 require protection of endpoint devices and restriction of access. Security Standards defines the hardening baselines and technical requirements that implement these controls.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity
rationale: A.5.24 requires defined incident management processes and roles, A.5.29 requires planned maintenance of security during disruption, and A.5.30 requires ICT continuity requirements and plans. Response & Resilience Standards provides the standardized procedures and criteria for these plans.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.1: Policies for information security
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.1 allows topic-specific policies and supporting rules, but ISO/IEC 27001 contains no requirement for AI model, data, or deployment standards. AI Standards is relevant only where AI systems are in ISMS scope; ISO/IEC 42001 is the closer standard.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements; A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.31 requires legal and regulatory requirements to be identified and met, and A.5.34 requires privacy and PII protection requirements to be identified and met. Data Privacy Compliance supplies that identification and oversight for privacy law; ISO/IEC 27701 covers the privacy program itself.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.32: Intellectual property rights
rationale: Intellectual Property (IP) Management supports A.5.32 because its IP inventory, OSS and third-party license tracking, ownership agreements, and infringement handling are the procedures A.5.32 requires to protect intellectual property rights and use proprietary software and data lawfully.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements; A.5.36: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
rationale: A.5.31 requires legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to information security to be identified, documented, and kept current, and A.5.36 requires compliance with them to be reviewed. Cybersecurity Regulatory Compliance maintains that obligations register and the continuous compliance checks.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.34 requires PII protection requirements to be identified and met through organization-wide processes. Privacy Program establishes the enterprise privacy management program that operates those processes; ISO/IEC 27701 is the standard that specifies the program.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 6.1.1: Actions to address risks and opportunities (general); 8.3: Information security risk treatment
rationale: Risk Management Framework supports 6.1.1 and 8.3 because the unified ERM framework determines the risks and opportunities the ISMS must address and plans actions for them (6.1.1), and its treatment of security, AI, and privacy risks operates the information security risk treatment plan (8.3).

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 6.1.2(a): Information security risk assessment (risk acceptance criteria)
rationale: Clause 6.1.2(a) requires the risk assessment process to establish and maintain risk acceptance criteria. Risk Appetite and Tolerance defines and approves those thresholds for each risk domain.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 6.1.2: Information security risk assessment; 6.1.3: Information security risk treatment; A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities; A.8.16: Monitoring activities
rationale: Risk-Management Program: Cybersecurity supports 6.1.2, 6.1.3, A.8.8, and A.8.16 because its risk evaluation and treatment planning implement the ISMS risk assessment and treatment processes, its vulnerability management with SLAs implements A.8.8, and its SIEM/XDR continuous monitoring implements A.8.16.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.19: Information security in supplier relationships; A.5.20: Addressing information security within supplier agreements; A.5.21: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain; A.5.22: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services; A.5.23: Information security for use of cloud services
rationale: A.5.19 to A.5.23 require supplier security risk to be managed through defined processes, agreements, ICT supply chain controls, ongoing monitoring, and cloud service requirements. Risk-Management Program: Third-Party establishes the program that governs vendor and partner risk end to end.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 4.3: Determining the scope of the information security management system
rationale: System Boundaries supports clause 4.3 because its maintained diagrams and inventories of in-scope and out-of-scope components, trust zones, interfaces, and third-party connections define the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS that 4.3 requires.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 4.1: Understanding the organization and its context
rationale: Clause 4.1 requires the organization to determine the external and internal issues relevant to its purpose that affect the ISMS. Mission Statement defines and communicates that purpose so ISMS objectives align to it.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 4.1: Understanding the organization and its context; 4.2: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties; 6.2: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
rationale: Clause 4.1 requires internal and external issues to be determined, 4.2 requires interested parties and their requirements to be identified, and 6.2 requires measurable information security objectives. Goals & Context translates mission and context into those risk-informed objectives.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.9: Inventory of information and other associated assets
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.9 requires an inventory of information and associated assets with owners, which can include AI systems. AI Scope identifies and risk-categorizes AI systems, but ISO/IEC 27001 has no AI-specific scoping requirement; ISO/IEC 42001 is the closer standard.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 4.3: Determining the scope of the information security management system; A.5.9: Inventory of information and other associated assets
rationale: Clause 4.3 requires the ISMS scope to be determined considering context, interested parties, and interfaces, and A.5.9 requires an owned inventory of assets. Security Scope decides which assets and environments the program protects and how protection is proportionate to criticality.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 4.2: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties; A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
rationale: Clause 4.2 requires the requirements of interested parties, including legal and contractual requirements, to be determined, and A.5.31 requires those requirements to be identified and documented. Regulatory Scope determines the applicable obligations the ISMS must address.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.32: Change management
rationale: A.8.32 requires changes to information processing facilities and systems to be subject to change management procedures. Change Management provides the risk assessment, approval, and audit trail for system, dataset, model, and configuration changes.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.25: Secure development life cycle; A.8.26: Application security requirements; A.8.27: Secure system architecture and engineering principles; A.8.28: Secure coding; A.8.31: Separation of development, test and production environments
rationale: A.8.25 requires rules for secure development, A.8.26 security requirements for applications, A.8.27 secure architecture principles, A.8.28 secure coding, and A.8.31 separation of development, test, and production environments. Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) embeds these practices in all development.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.6.1: Screening; A.6.2: Terms and conditions of employment; A.6.4: Disciplinary process; A.6.5: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment; A.6.6: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
rationale: A.6.1 requires screening, A.6.2 security terms in employment contracts, A.6.4 a disciplinary process, A.6.5 responsibilities after termination or change, and A.6.6 confidentiality agreements. Human Resources operates these practices through hiring, role changes, and departures.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.34 requires PII protection requirements to be identified and met, which needs a decision-making body. Privacy Oversight Committee provides that governance, but ISO/IEC 27001 does not require a privacy committee; ISO/IEC 27701 is the closer standard.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 5.1: Leadership and commitment; 5.3: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities; 9.3: Management review
rationale: Clause 5.1 requires leadership commitment, 5.3 assigned ISMS roles and authorities, and 9.3 management review of ISMS performance. Security Oversight Committee is the governance body that prioritizes and reviews cybersecurity, threat, and resilience programs on behalf of leadership.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 9.1: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
rationale: Clause 9.1 requires the organization to determine what to monitor and measure, the methods, timing, and who evaluates results. Performance Metrics defines and reports those measures across security, privacy, AI governance, and risk.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.19: Information security in supplier relationships; A.5.20: Addressing information security within supplier agreements; A.5.21: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain; A.5.22: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services; A.5.23: Information security for use of cloud services
rationale: A.5.19 requires supplier risk management processes, A.5.20 security requirements in agreements, A.5.21 ICT supply chain controls, A.5.22 monitoring and review of supplier services, and A.5.23 cloud service requirements. Third-Party Risk Management performs vendor assessment, contracting, and oversight under these controls.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 6.1.2: Information security risk assessment; A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities; A.8.16: Monitoring activities; A.8.27: Secure system architecture and engineering principles; A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: Clause 6.1.2 requires the information security risk assessment to be repeated at planned intervals and on significant change. Cybersecurity Risk Management continuously evaluates threats, vulnerabilities, and exposure to feed that assessment, identifying vulnerabilities through scanning, penetration testing, and red teaming (A.8.8, A.8.29), threat modeling critical systems (A.8.27), and maintaining continuous monitoring (A.8.16).

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 9.3: Management review
rationale: Clause 9.3 requires management review inputs on ISMS performance, nonconformities, monitoring results, audit results, and risk assessment results. Reporting delivers that structured, risk-informed reporting to executives, the Board, and regulators.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.9: Inventory of information and other associated assets; A.5.12: Classification of information; A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities; A.8.9: Configuration management
rationale: System Asset Management supports A.5.9, A.5.12, A.8.8, and A.8.9 because its authoritative CMDB with owners implements the asset inventory, its classification and security categorization implements classification of information, its linkage to scanners and patch telemetry supports vulnerability management, and its change-driven lifecycle records support configuration management.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.6.7: Remote working; A.8.1: User endpoint devices
rationale: A.6.7 requires security measures for remote working, and A.8.1 requires information on user endpoint devices to be protected, including personally owned devices. BYOD Asset Management enrols, restricts, and monitors personally owned devices that access organizational data.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.9: Inventory of information and other associated assets; A.5.12: Classification of information; A.5.14: Information transfer
rationale: A.5.9 requires an inventory of information assets, A.5.12 requires information to be classified, and A.5.14 requires rules for information transfer. Data Mapping documents end-to-end data flows for collection, processing, storage, sharing, and deletion so these controls can be applied to each flow.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 6.1.2: Information security risk assessment
rationale: Risk Identification supports 6.1.2 because identifying risks across cyber, privacy, safety, ethics, and AI is the risk identification step of the information security risk assessment process defined in 6.1.2.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.2: Information security roles and responsibilities; A.6.3: Information security awareness, education and training; A.8.2: Privileged access rights; A.8.27: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
rationale: Insider Threat supports A.5.2, A.6.3, A.8.2, and A.8.27 because the insider threat program assigns oversight roles across HR, Security, and Legal (A.5.2), relies on awareness training (A.6.3), maintains a register of privileged and sensitive-access roles (A.8.2), and depends on architecture that limits the reach of a single insider (A.8.27).

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.21: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain; A.5.22: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services; A.5.23: Information security for use of cloud services
rationale: A.5.21 requires risks in the ICT products and services supply chain to be managed, A.5.22 requires supplier services to be monitored and reviewed, and A.5.23 requires security requirements for cloud services. Supply Chain Risk identifies and manages risk from suppliers of software, models, datasets, and cloud services.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.16: Monitoring activities
rationale: Partial alignment: A.8.16 requires networks, systems, and applications to be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken. Security Thresholds defines the alarm thresholds and decision criteria that make that monitoring actionable, but ISO/IEC 27001 does not itself require threshold definitions.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.7: Threat intelligence
rationale: A.5.7 requires information about security threats to be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence. Threat Management continuously identifies, assesses, and tracks threats to information systems and AI assets to inform defenses.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.6.3: Information security awareness, education and training; 7.3: Awareness
rationale: A.6.3 requires personnel to receive security awareness, education, and training, and clause 7.3 requires awareness of the policy and of their contribution to the ISMS. Cybersecurity Training delivers the foundational and advanced awareness program that covers phishing, social engineering, malware, and insider threats.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 7.2: Competence; 7.3: Awareness; A.6.3: Information security awareness, education and training
rationale: Clause 7.2 requires persons doing ISMS work to be competent, 7.3 requires awareness of the policy and their role, and A.6.3 requires role-relevant training. Governance Training builds that competence in leadership, risk owners, and committee members.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.12: Classification of information; A.5.13: Labelling of information; A.5.10: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets; A.7.10: Storage media
rationale: A.5.12 requires information to be classified by sensitivity, A.5.13 requires labelling per the classification scheme, A.5.10 requires handling rules for assets, and A.7.10 requires storage media to be managed through its lifecycle. Classification & Handling applies the labels and handling protocols these controls require.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.24: Use of cryptography
rationale: A.8.24 requires rules for the effective use of cryptography, including key management, to be defined and implemented. Cryptographic Management governs algorithm selection, key lifecycle, and the use of encryption for data and AI models.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.1: User endpoint devices; A.8.7: Protection against malware; A.8.9: Configuration management; A.8.19: Installation of software on operational systems
rationale: A.8.1 requires protection of user endpoint devices, A.8.7 protection against malware, A.8.9 established configurations, and A.8.19 control over software installation on operational systems. Endpoint Security hardens endpoints and servers and deploys anti-malware and EDR to meet these controls.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.15: Access control; A.5.16: Identity management; A.5.17: Authentication information; A.5.18: Access rights; A.8.2: Privileged access rights; A.8.5: Secure authentication
rationale: A.5.15 requires access control rules, A.5.16 identity lifecycle management, A.5.17 control of authentication information, A.5.18 provisioning and review of access rights, A.8.2 restriction of privileged access, and A.8.5 secure authentication. Identity Management enforces least privilege and separation of duties for human and machine identities.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.20: Networks security; A.8.21: Security of network services; A.8.22: Segregation of networks; A.8.23: Web filtering
rationale: A.8.20 requires networks to be secured and controlled, A.8.21 security of network services, A.8.22 segregation of networks, and A.8.23 web filtering. Network Security designs and enforces the zero-trust segmentation and traffic controls that implement these requirements.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII; A.8.11: Data masking; A.8.12: Data leakage prevention
rationale: Partial alignment: A.5.34 requires PII protection requirements to be met, A.8.11 requires data masking in line with access and business requirements, and A.8.12 requires data leakage prevention. Privacy Controls implements privacy-enhancing technologies that satisfy these technical measures; ISO/IEC 27701 specifies the full privacy control set.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.9: Configuration management; A.8.19: Installation of software on operational systems; A.8.31: Separation of development, test and production environments; A.8.32: Change management
rationale: A.8.9 requires secure configurations to be established and monitored, A.8.19 control of software installation, A.8.31 separation of environments, and A.8.32 change management. Platform Security hardens cloud, container, and MLOps platforms and protects build and deploy planes under these controls.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.7.1: Physical security perimeters; A.7.2: Physical entry; A.7.3: Securing offices, rooms and facilities; A.7.4: Physical security monitoring; A.7.10: Storage media; A.7.14: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
rationale: Physical Access Controls supports A.7.1 to A.7.4, A.7.10, and A.7.14 because its perimeter and entry controls, secured server rooms with CCTV, chain-of-custody media handling, and certified disposal implement physical perimeters, entry, secure areas, physical monitoring, storage media protection, and secure disposal.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.7.5: Protecting against physical and environmental threats; A.7.8: Equipment siting and protection; A.7.11: Supporting utilities; A.7.12: Cabling security; A.7.13: Equipment maintenance
rationale: A.7.5 requires protection against physical and environmental threats, A.7.8 secure siting of equipment, A.7.11 protection of supporting utilities, A.7.12 cabling security, and A.7.13 equipment maintenance. Environment Controls provides the power, fire, HVAC, water, and maintenance safeguards these controls require.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.7.5: Protecting against physical and environmental threats; A.7.10: Storage media; A.7.11: Supporting utilities
rationale: Safety & Security supports A.7.5, A.7.10, and A.7.11 because its emergency and evacuation procedures protect personnel and assets against physical threats, its secure evacuation of data and media protects storage media in transit, and its emergency power-off for compute clusters is part of managing supporting utilities.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity; A.8.14: Redundancy of information processing facilities
rationale: Resilience Controls supports A.5.29, A.5.30, and A.8.14 because its defined RTO/RPO, resilient architecture, graceful-degradation modes, and recovery testing maintain information security during disruption, establish ICT readiness for business continuity, and implement redundancy of information processing facilities.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity
rationale: A.5.29 requires the organization to plan how to maintain information security during disruption, and A.5.30 requires ICT readiness for business continuity based on continuity objectives. Business Continuity maintains critical services through BIA-driven strategies, workarounds, and communications.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity; A.8.13: Information backup; A.8.14: Redundancy of information processing facilities
rationale: A.5.30 requires ICT continuity plans to be implemented and tested, A.8.13 requires backups to be maintained and regularly tested, and A.8.14 requires redundancy of processing facilities. Disaster Recovery restores systems, data, and AI pipelines to target RTO/RPO using immutable, tested backups.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.21: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain; A.5.23: Information security for use of cloud services; A.8.30: Outsourced development
rationale: A.5.21 requires security risks in the ICT supply chain to be managed, A.5.23 requires security for acquisition and use of cloud services, and A.8.30 requires outsourced development to be directed and reviewed. Supply Chain ensures provenance and integrity of third-party components, models, APIs, and open source.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.25: Secure development life cycle; A.8.26: Application security requirements; A.8.27: Secure system architecture and engineering principles; A.8.28: Secure coding; A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: A.8.25 requires secure development rules, A.8.26 application security requirements, A.8.27 secure architecture principles, A.8.28 secure coding, and A.8.29 security testing in development and acceptance. Secure Development integrates these practices from design through release and operations.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.16: Monitoring activities
rationale: A.8.16 requires networks, systems, and applications to be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken. Anomaly Detection provides the statistical, heuristic, and model-based detection of unusual system, data, and AI behaviour that this monitoring relies on.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.15: Logging; A.8.16: Monitoring activities; A.8.17: Clock synchronization
rationale: A.8.15 requires logs of activities and events to be produced, stored, and analysed, A.8.16 requires continuous monitoring for anomalous behaviour, and A.8.17 requires synchronized clocks so log correlation is reliable. Continuous Monitoring provides the automated monitoring of security, privacy, and AI performance that these controls require.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.16: Monitoring activities; A.5.7: Threat intelligence
rationale: A.8.16 requires monitoring to detect anomalous behaviour and possible security incidents, and A.5.7 requires threat intelligence to be used to detect and reduce threats. IOC Detection identifies indicators of compromise across enterprise and AI systems using that intelligence.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.25: Assessment and decision on information security events; A.5.26: Response to information security incidents; A.5.27: Learning from information security incidents; A.5.28: Collection of evidence
rationale: A.5.24 requires incident management planning and preparation, A.5.25 assessment of events and decision on incidents, A.5.26 response per documented procedures, A.5.27 learning from incidents, and A.5.28 collection of evidence. Incident Management operates this end-to-end identification, analysis, containment, and recovery process.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.22: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
rationale: A.5.22 requires the organization to regularly monitor, review, evaluate, and manage change in supplier information security practices and service delivery. Monitor Third Parties performs that continuous monitoring of the vendor and partner ecosystem.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.35: Independent review of information security; A.5.36: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security; A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities
rationale: Performing Security Assessments supports A.5.35, A.5.36, and A.8.8 because independent, systematic security testing of controls produces the independent review evidence for A.5.35, verifies compliance with security policies and standards under A.5.36, and identifies technical vulnerabilities for treatment under A.8.8.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities; A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: A.8.8 requires information about technical vulnerabilities to be obtained and exposure evaluated, and A.8.29 requires security testing in development and acceptance. Penetration Testing simulates adversarial attacks against systems and models to find exploitable weaknesses and evaluate resilience.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities
rationale: A.8.8 requires technical vulnerabilities to be identified, exposure evaluated, and appropriate measures taken. Vulnerability Testing performs the scanning and mitigation tracking across systems, applications, and AI components that A.8.8 requires.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity; A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation
rationale: A.5.30 requires ICT continuity plans to be exercised and tested, A.5.29 requires planned maintenance of security during disruption, and A.5.24 requires incident management preparation. Tabletop Exercises (BCDR) tests continuity, recovery, and response readiness through structured simulations.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.28: Secure coding; A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: A.8.28 requires secure coding principles to be applied, and A.8.29 requires security testing to be defined and implemented in the development life cycle. Code Scanning applies static and dynamic analysis so application and AI codebases are free of known defects and insecure configurations.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.7: Threat intelligence
rationale: A.5.7 requires information about information security threats to be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence that is used in defenses. Threat Intelligence integrates actionable intelligence, including AI-specific adversarial tactics, into detection and defense programs.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.5: Contact with authorities; A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements; A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation
rationale: A.5.5 requires contact with relevant authorities to be established and maintained, A.5.31 requires regulatory requirements including breach notification to be identified and met, and A.5.24 requires incident procedures to include reporting. Regulatory Reporting meets breach-reporting obligations to regulators in time and content.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.5: Contact with authorities; A.5.28: Collection of evidence
rationale: A.5.5 requires contact with authorities, including law enforcement, to be maintained, and A.5.28 requires evidence to be collected and preserved in a form usable in legal proceedings. Law Enforcement Partners engages authorities promptly when criminal or nation-state activity is suspected and supports them with preserved evidence.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.6: Contact with special interest groups; A.5.7: Threat intelligence
rationale: A.5.6 requires contact with special interest groups and security forums to be maintained, and A.5.7 requires threat intelligence to be shared where appropriate. Information-Sharing Communities shares sanitized threat intelligence with peers and ISACs to strengthen collective defense.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII; A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements; A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation
rationale: A.5.34 requires PII protection requirements, including breach notification to individuals, to be identified and met, A.5.31 requires legal requirements to be met, and A.5.24 requires incident procedures to cover communication. Privacy Notification Requirements notifies affected individuals per legal and contractual obligations after a verified breach.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.6.8: Information security event reporting; A.6.3: Information security awareness, education and training
rationale: A.5.24 requires incident management procedures to define communication, A.6.8 requires personnel to know how to report events, and A.6.3 requires awareness of incident procedures. Personnel informs affected teams during incidents and distributes guidance so staff know what to do and how to report.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.4: Management responsibilities; 5.1: Leadership and commitment
rationale: A.5.24 requires incident management roles and escalation to be defined, A.5.4 requires management to require personnel to apply security procedures, and clause 5.1 requires leadership to direct the ISMS. Top Management provides executive briefings on incident status, impact, options, and decisions.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.26: Response to information security incidents; A.8.15: Logging
rationale: A.5.24 requires defined incident roles and processes, A.5.26 requires response according to documented procedures, and A.8.15 requires activities during incidents to be logged. Incident Response Team maintains synchronized internal communication and a single source of truth during active incidents.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.26: Response to information security incidents; A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
rationale: A.5.24 requires incident procedures to address communication, A.5.26 requires response including communication to relevant parties, and A.5.31 requires legal and contractual disclosure obligations to be met. Public Updates / Disclosures manages approved public and media statements that balance transparency and risk.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity; A.5.26: Response to information security incidents
rationale: A.5.29 and A.5.30 require continuity and ICT readiness during disruption, including communication with interested parties, and A.5.26 requires incident response to include recovery. Recovery Activity & Restoration provides partners and customers timely updates on restoration and remediation status.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.26: Response to information security incidents; A.5.28: Collection of evidence
rationale: A.5.26 requires incidents to be responded to according to documented procedures, which include containment, and A.5.28 requires evidence to be identified, collected, and preserved. Containment isolates affected assets, blocks malicious activity, and preserves evidence for investigation.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.26: Response to information security incidents; A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities
rationale: A.5.26 requires incident response procedures that remove the cause of the incident, and A.8.8 requires measures to be taken against identified technical vulnerabilities. Eradication removes malicious artifacts, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations that caused the incident.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity; A.8.13: Information backup
rationale: A.5.30 requires ICT readiness for business continuity so services can be restored, and A.8.13 requires backups to be maintained and tested so information can be recovered. Disaster Recovery restores systems and data from a clean, trusted state using verified, immutable backups after an incident.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.29: Information security during disruption; A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity
rationale: A.5.29 requires information security to be maintained during disruption, and A.5.30 requires ICT continuity to meet business continuity requirements. Business Continuity maintains critical operations during incident response and recovery so customer commitments continue to be met.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation; A.5.25: Assessment and decision on information security events; A.5.26: Response to information security incidents; A.5.27: Learning from information security incidents; A.5.28: Collection of evidence; A.6.8: Information security event reporting
rationale: A.5.24 to A.5.28 require incident management planning, event assessment, documented response, learning, and evidence collection, and A.6.8 requires timely reporting of events. Incident Response: Cybersecurity coordinates the technical response across infrastructure, endpoints, networks, applications, and third parties under these controls.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.5.27: Learning from information security incidents; 10.2: Nonconformity and corrective action
rationale: A.5.27 requires knowledge gained from incidents to be used to strengthen controls, and clause 10.2 requires nonconformities to be corrected and their causes eliminated. Incident Lessons Learned ensures every incident or near miss produces measurable control enhancement.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 9.2: Internal audit; A.5.35: Independent review of information security; A.5.36: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
rationale: Clause 9.2 requires audits that determine whether the ISMS conforms to the standard, A.5.35 requires independent review of information security at planned intervals, and A.5.36 requires compliance review. External Audit: Security Audit obtains independent validation of the ISMS, such as certification audit, that satisfies the independence these controls require.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.6.8: Information security event reporting; A.5.24: Information security incident management planning and preparation
rationale: A.6.8 requires a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected security events in a timely way, and A.5.24 requires those reports to feed incident management. Reporting Channels provides safe, accessible channels for employees, customers, and users to report risks, incidents, and concerns.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 9.2.1: Internal audit (general); 9.2.2: Internal audit programme; A.5.35: Independent review of information security
rationale: Clause 9.2.1 requires internal audits to determine ISMS conformity and effectiveness, 9.2.2 requires an audit programme with impartial auditors, and A.5.35 requires independent review. Internal Audit: Security Audit independently assesses ISMS control design and operating effectiveness.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 9.2.1: Internal audit (general); 9.2.2: Internal audit programme; A.5.35: Independent review of information security
rationale: Internal Audit supports ISO/IEC 27001 clauses 9.2.1 and 9.2.2 and control A.5.35 because its charter, risk-based annual audit plan, independent execution, and tracked corrective actions are the internal audit programme the ISMS must run, and its independence requirement provides the independent review of information security that A.5.35 requires.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance; A.8.33: Test information
rationale: A.8.29 requires security testing processes to be defined and implemented in the development life cycle, and A.8.33 requires test information to be selected and protected. Testing plans and executes functional, security, reliability, and safety tests for systems and AI components before release.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: Partial alignment: A.8.29 requires security testing in development and acceptance. Evaluation assesses performance, safety, and harms across operating contexts, which goes beyond the security testing A.8.29 requires; the overlap is acceptance testing of security and reliability.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): 9.1: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation; A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: Clause 9.1 requires evaluation of ISMS performance and control effectiveness, and A.8.29 requires acceptance testing against security requirements. Verification confirms that implemented systems meet stated requirements and that controls operate as designed.

ISO/IEC 27001 Control Item(s): A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance
rationale: Partial alignment: A.8.29 requires acceptance testing before systems move to production. Validation confirms the system achieves its intended use without unacceptable risk, which includes but extends beyond the security acceptance testing A.8.29 requires.
